methods.label: Show that triangle shapes repeat every four steps
methods.explanation:
Because the requested points have large indices, look for a repeating triangle shape rather than locate every point. We will show that advancing all three indices by four produces a similar triangle with corresponding vertices in the same order.

Take three consecutive points \(X=A_n\), \(Y=A_{n+1}\), and \(Z=A_{n+2}\). The next four points are
\[
U=A_{n+3},\quad V=A_{n+4},\quad W=A_{n+5},\quad T=A_{n+6}.
\]
By the given rule, \(U\) is the midpoint of \(XY\), \(V\) is the midpoint of \(YZ\), \(W\) is the midpoint of \(ZU\), and \(T\) is the midpoint of \(UV\).

These midpoint relationships reveal all three sides of triangle \(VWT\). In triangle \(ZYU\), segment \(VW\) joins two side midpoints, so
\[
VW=\frac12 YU=\frac14 XY.
\]
In triangle \(UZV\), segment \(WT\) likewise joins two side midpoints, giving
\[
WT=\frac12 ZV=\frac14 YZ.
\]
Finally, \(UV\) is a midsegment of triangle \(XYZ\), and \(T\) is its midpoint, so
\[
TV=\frac12 UV=\frac14 ZX.
\]
Thus \(\triangle VWT\sim\triangle XYZ\) by SSS similarity, with correspondences \(V\leftrightarrow X\), \(W\leftrightarrow Y\), and \(T\leftrightarrow Z\). Starting from a nondegenerate triangle, each four-step triangle is therefore nondegenerate as well.

Now \(43=3+10\cdot4\). Applying this correspondence ten times shows that
\[
\angle A_{44}A_{45}A_{43}=\angle A_4A_5A_3.
\]
It remains to find this early angle. Points \(A_4\) and \(A_5\) are the midpoints of \(A_1A_2\) and \(A_2A_3\). The midsegment theorem and the equal original sides show that triangle \(A_2A_4A_5\) is equilateral. Hence \(\angle A_4A_5A_2=60^\circ\). Since \(A_5\) lies between \(A_2\) and \(A_3\), the rays \(A_5A_2\) and \(A_5A_3\) are opposite, so
\[
\angle A_4A_5A_3=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ.
\]
Therefore the requested angle is \(\boxed{120^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
